claims.text: Standard layer-by-layer additive manufacturing of CoCrFeMnNi components produces inhomogeneous microstructures.
Standard additively manufactured CoCrFeMnNi components contain micro-porosity.
Residual-stress gradients in standard additively manufactured CoCrFeMnNi components cause dimensional deviations.
Residual-stress gradients and fabrication-induced defects compromise the mechanical properties of additively manufactured CoCrFeMnNi components.
In-situ laser re-melting after each deposited layer, combined with thermal modeling and real-time temperature monitoring, will homogenize and refine the CoCrFeMnNi microstructure.
The proposed intervention will reduce porosity in additively manufactured CoCrFeMnNi components.
The proposed intervention will minimize residual-stress gradients at inter-layer boundaries.
Controlled in-situ re-melting homogenizes temperature profiles and facilitates complete fusion at layer interfaces.
Rapid solidification induced by a pulsed laser refines the grain structure.
Pulsed-laser re-melting heals microscale defects.
Real-time monitoring can manage the additional heat input sufficiently to prevent undesirable thermal stresses.
Real-time monitoring can prevent abnormal grain growth during in-situ laser re-melting.
The microstructural and thermal effects of the intervention will improve dimensional precision.
The microstructural and thermal effects of the intervention will improve mechanical strength.
The intervention will reduce dimensional deviations by at least 30% relative to conventional additive manufacturing.
The intervention will improve yield strength by approximately 20% relative to conventional additive manufacturing.
The intervention will improve fatigue resistance by approximately 20% relative to conventional additive manufacturing.
The predicted benefits require an inert atmosphere containing less than 1% oxygen and a substrate temperature of approximately 300–400°C.
Laser parameters designed for a melt-pool depth of approximately 50 µm can provide the intended re-melting effect while avoiding excessive heat accumulation.
Failure to maintain the specified thermal conditions may eliminate the benefits or introduce new defects.
